intelligence.enrichment: Night-sky visibility depends on a clear dark sky, low light pollution, an open viewing area, the observer's place on Earth, and the date and time for the chosen object. Clearer, darker, object-appropriate conditions make more sky objects visible; city lights, clouds, blocked views, or the wrong place or time reduce what can be seen. The learner correctly applies this rule: Night-sky visibility depends on a clear dark sky, low light pollution, an open viewing area, the observer's place on Earth, and the date and time for the chosen object. If an object exists in the sky, it can be seen from any place whenever it is night.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 6 Science question. Chapter: Beyond Earth. The student must decide: Decide whether a chosen star, constellation, or planet can actually be observed from a given place, date, time, and sky condition. Use an Indian school or home setting and Indian names. Keep the source language register. Change the numbers, materials, or everyday situation. Do not copy the source stem. Recalculate the key. Do not print mix-up labels, hinge codes, node codes, or the word CANDIDATE.
